coverage.category: 1. Household employers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K03. Sources: ~11,300 domestic workers/yr, ~10% INPS-registered, ICIEG/UN Women draft domestic-work regulation not yet confirmed adopted (https://www.dn.pt/lusa/interior/maioria-das-empregadas-domesticas-cabo-verdianas-nao-tem-contrato-nem-protecao-social-9066788.html). ILO Feb 2026 notes domestic workers are in the employee scheme; an INPS resolution amending Res. 58/2020 separates 'prestador de serviço doméstico' (paid per day/hour) from 'trabalhador doméstico'. A formalisation drive would strengthen K03.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: No search spent; budget used on country-specific and higher-priority categories.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.found: No search spent. The exchange-office search showed that BCV regulates operations on gold, but no dealer-specific rule was found.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: No dedicated search. The fish-export search surfaced Lei 30/VIII/2013 (animal health) and DR 12/2020 (animal-product hygiene) as the framework; no duty detail checked.

coverage.found: No dedicated search. See category 6 for the framework laws seen.

coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: The ERIS regulator took over ARFA, DGF and IGS functions in 2019 and covers human and veterinary medicines. No vet-specific recurring duty found. Source: https://expressodasilhas.cv/topico/eris

coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: No general licensing regime for temporary-work agencies found. Only a student temporary-work scheme run by FICASE, which is not relevant. Unverified whether a general regime exists.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies
coverage.found: Non-profits are registered at the Conservatória de Registo das Pessoas Coletivas under Lei 25/VI/2003; OSCD law covers development NGOs. No periodic reporting duty confirmed. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: The general road transport regime DL 19/2022 was amended by DL 27/2025 (BO 19 Aug 2025: sanctions, clandestine transport, driver must show licence copy) and DL 15/2026 of 20 March 2026 (also revises rent-a-car access). Operators are mostly sole traders or single-person companies. See candidates. Sources: https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=100451, https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/33965

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Exchange offices (agências de câmbio) need BCV authorisation, must be a SA or Lda, have minimum capital and register with the BCV. This is a formal and capital-heavy segment, so weak. Street vendors not searched. Source: https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/2541

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections
coverage.found: Driving schools: no Cabo Verde rule found. Vehicle inspection is run by a concession (MADINSP, exclusive) under DGTR. Restaurants, bars and food: IGAE inspects; the permanent licensing regime was not found. Nothing actionable.

coverage.category: 21. Fuel stations and fuel or LPG distributors
coverage.found: ARME sets monthly maximum prices (butane per cylinder, 12.5 kg at 1,770 CVE in Aug 2026) and the Sistema Petrolífero Nacional is DL 56/2010. No station licensing or periodic-return rule found. The name ARFA in the brief is outdated; ERIS replaced it for health. Few operators, so unlikely. Source: https://forbesafricalusofona.com/?p=177055

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: No search spent. Cabo Verde has no major export commodity of this type; the sugar-cane spirit sector is covered under 31.

coverage.category: 23. Co-operatives, credit unions and savings groups
coverage.found: The current co-operative law and annual reporting duties were not found. Old texts only; a 2017 text suggests the Código das Sociedades Comerciais applies to credit co-operatives. Unverified.

coverage.category: 24. Private clinics, labs and other health providers that bill insurers or state schemes
coverage.found: ERIS licenses health establishments. A decree published in BO 57, 12 May 2026 (PDF metadata says DL 33/2026) appears to set the licensing, conformity declaration, opening and operating regime, but its text was unreadable and the match to health establishments is not confirmed. INPS covers about 43% of the population; I found no INPS convention regime with private clinics. See candidate. Source: https://boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/DownloadAct?id=101356

coverage.category: 25. Pharmacies, medicine importers, and users of controlled chemicals or precursors
coverage.found: ERIS licenses pharmacies, including via a published tender process. No recurring small-business reporting duty found. Source: https://expressodasilhas.cv/topico/eris

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Private security is supervised by DGAI. The 2021 thesis says oversight is weak and mostly pedagogic. No electronic reporting duty found. Cleaning and manpower agencies: nothing found.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: No search spent.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: The AML law is Lei 120/VIII/2016 and lawyers are DNFBPs per the GIABA mutual evaluation. Entity list, thresholds and the reporting channel to the UIF were not confirmed. Searches returned mostly Portuguese material. See candidate.

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K01 and K05. Not searched, as the known list already covers it.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules
coverage.found: Fish exports need a sanitary or veterinary certificate (Portaria 19/2007, replaced by 13/2009, which FAOLEX lists as revoked) and a catch certificate (Portaria 48/2009). Exports go mostly to the EU. Exporters are few and processor-sized. Source: https://leap.unep.org/en/countries/cv/national-legislation/order-no-132009-sanitary-certificate-fish-products-export

coverage.category: 31. Sugar-cane spirit (grogue) distilleries and traders
coverage.found: Regime DL 11/2015; 388 stills (99 in Ribeira Grande, Santo Antão); IGAE inspections, with 209 of 363 inspected plants deemed licensable; cane cutting only January to May; 2025 inspection campaign in Santo Antão and Santiago; many small distillers stopped after the post-COVID rules. See candidate.

coverage.category: 32. Fiscal stamps (selos fiscais) for tobacco and alcohol producers and importers
coverage.found: A new selagem portaria (replaces a 62-year-old paper regime) requires stamp use to be recorded on a traceability platform. Whether grogue is covered is unconfirmed. Source: https://forbesafricalusofona.com/?p=79319

coverage.category: 33. Rent-a-car, taxi and public-transport licences (DL 19/2022 as amended)
coverage.found: See category 18 and candidates.

coverage.category: 34. Renewable microproduction and self-generation (DL 1/2011, DL 54/2018)
coverage.found: Prior registration at the Direção Geral de Energia and later inspection; installations under 400 W are exempt from prior registration. Buyers are installers and households, with no recurring duty confirmed. Weak. Source: https://www.mirandalawfirm.com/download/1183/d8179971c4669e2c62903476e317a6dd/ln_cabo_verde_julho_a_outubro_de_2018_pt.pdf

coverage.category: 35. Vehicle technical inspection
coverage.found: Exclusive concession (MADINSP) under the DGTR, per a Boletim Oficial contract. Current status unconfirmed. Not a candidate.

coverage.category: 36. Fishing licences and artisanal fishing
coverage.found: Commercial fishing needs a licence (a 2023 regulation sets obligations for licensed vessels). Artisanal-fishing rules and a fishers register were not found. Unverified.

coverage.category: 37. Business formalisation and licensing simplification (DL 21/2011 and later)
coverage.found: No 2024-2026 general licensing or RCBE-type obligation found for Cabo Verde. Searches returned Portuguese results.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: One search; no Cabo Verde scrap-dealer licence or register found (results were Brazilian). Likely falls under general commercial licensing and waste regime DL 56/2015. Nothing new beyond that. Unverified that a dedicated register exists.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No second-hand-dealer register found. A Boletim Oficial text (boe.incv.cv/Bulletins/Download/12714, date and number not confirmed) opened pawn lending to any commercial company, credit institution or social-solidarity institution. AML law Lei 120/VIII/2016 exists, but whether it covers pawnbrokers or second-hand dealers is unconfirmed. Likely very few operators.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: No dealer-specific licence or hallmark/register rule found. Results covered only BCV's own gold reserves. Whether AML law 120/VIII/2016 reaches precious-metal dealers is unchecked.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No dismantler, end-of-life vehicle or used-parts rule found. Only the vehicle-standards rule RVAC (DR 7/2020, amended by DL 15/2026, March 2026), which covers vehicle characteristics and inspection, not dismantling. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: No livestock-market, movement-permit or trader register found. The framework is Lei 30/VIII/2013 and DR 10/2020 (slaughter conditions for animals, applies to producers, traders and keepers) plus DR 12/2020. Duty detail not read.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: DR 10/2020 of 25 Sept (technical procedures and conditions for slaughtering domestic animals, ante/post-mortem inspection at abattoirs) and DR 12/2020 of 8 Oct (hygiene of animal products). Butcher-shop registration/licence rules not found (the only butcher-register text was Portuguese). Articles on authorisations and records not read.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: One search; no Cabo Verde apiculture register, honey certification rule or association found. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: DL 47/2021 of 10 June 2021 (BO I Série n.59) revoked all private irrigation-only borehole, well and gallery licences and some mixed-use ones. It phases the systems into the state irrigation company Agua de Rega (AdR), with ANAS approving the list. So the private-licence duty is being removed, not created. Driller-licence rules not found. Borehole solar tender: Resolução 52/2026 (BO n.32, 17 Mar 2026) concerns ANAS procurement only.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Waste management (collection, transport, treatment) falls under DL 56/2015, which has a licensing/concession regime and the SIRES waste information system. ANAS is the authority. Septic-sludge-specific rules, licence steps and operator reporting not confirmed. Waste list in DL 65/2018.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Nothing found. No Cabo Verde lift, boiler or pressure-equipment regime surfaced (results were Brazilian NR-13 and Portuguese). Treat as no evidence rather than no rule.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: Sector framework: Decreto Legislativo 5/2018 (legal regime of water and sanitation services), DL 26/2016 (tariff policy), ARME tariff regulation. Irrigation systems formerly licensed to private owners and irrigator associations are moving to AdR (2020 law and DL 47/2021). No rules found for community drinking-water systems or standpipe associations.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: One search; no current Cabo Verde dealer licence or applicator certification found. Only an older advisory commission on agricultural phytopharmaceuticals and an old plant-health import/export decree. Unverified.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: DL 34/2016 of 5 May 2016 (BO I Série n.34) governs access to and exercise of the funeral activity. Funeral agencies must register with the municipality (electronic registration, registration number shown on documents, changes reported within 30 days), must offer a basic social funeral at a maximum price, must have minimum staff, and face fines (some 50,000 to 300,000 escudos) and registration suspension; registration fee goes to municipal licences. Mutual associations may also act. Private cemetery concessions and funeral centres are allowed. Small buyer pool; see ledger.

coverage.category: 22. Grain, coffee, cocoa and other commodity traders, millers and warehouses
coverage.found: Wheat flour liberalised (DL 84/2005); DL 29/2002 removed operator duties (warehouses in every council, guarantee deposit, annual supply programme). State price compensation for maize, wheat and oils (2022 onward); silo capacity to rise from 14,000 to 32,000 t via a private firm in Santiago. No current operator register or reporting duty found. coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers
coverage.found: Quarries and inert extraction: DL 3/2015 (mineral masses; quarry licences, rehabilitation plans PARP, guarantee deposit art. 44), amended by DL 34/2021 and DL 16/2023 of 16 May; DL 18/2016 on sand extraction and dredging by public tender; Council of Ministers suspended beach-sand authorisations; strategy ENEI 2025-2030 targets 70% cut in illegal extraction and one licensed quarry per inhabited island. Contractor licensing: alvarás from the Comissão de Alvarás (Decreto 87/89, classes with maximum work values), seen only in 2006-2009 gazettes; current regime unconfirmed. Local-content/site-register rules not found.

result.reason: DL 15/2026 (BO 33, 20-03-2026) exists and amends DL 19/2022 (general road transport regime). Its PDF text was compressed and unreadable to the fetch tool, so the operative articles are unread. Search summaries say it eases licence access to widen the number of rent-a-car operators. That is a one-off liberalisation. I found no recurring reporting duty, deadline, fleet register or penalty. No operator count and no competing software were found. The duty looks like an occasional licence or alvará with the transport directorate, not a recurring workflow. The buyers are few and scattered. Weak fit.

The duty is real in outline. A search summary says DL 33/2026 (BO I Série n.º 57, 12 May 2026) sets a licence/declaração de conformidade regime for all health-care establishments, with ERIS supervising. The PDF text is unreadable, so I could not confirm the transition deadline, recurring declarations, penalties or fees. Licensing looks like a one-off or occasional filing at opening or modification, not a frequent workflow. The preamble says typologies will be regulated later. No provider count was found, and the market is probably a few hundred providers at most. Competition was not shown, but no local product was found. Weak recurrence and a tiny market keep the score at 3.

The duty is real. DL 3/2015 as amended by DL 34/2021 and DL 16/2023 requires quarry licences, PARP rehabilitation plans and a guarantee deposit (art. 44). DL 18/2016 covers sand extraction. The market is tiny and mostly informal: the ENEI 2025-2030 (Resolução 59/2026) counts 444 extraction sites in 2023, with only a small share formally licensed. A licensed-quarry count, a state register and 2024-26 amendments were not found. No competing software or portal turned up in 2 searches. The weak spots are the few buyers, filings that are occasional rather than recurring, limited willingness to pay, and a regime in flux. I did not open the legal texts. I did not confirm the current art. 44 wording or penalties.
